title: Ponerse, volverse, hacerse: verbs of change
summary: Spanish has no single verb for 'to become': ponerse for a sudden mood, volverse for a change of character, hacerse for a chosen path, quedarse for the result, convertirse en and llegar a ser for transformations and goals.
focus: Choosing the right verb of change: ponerse, volverse, hacerse, quedarse, convertirse en, llegar a ser
content:
## Ponerse: a sudden, passing change

Spanish has no single verb for *to become*. The verb depends on how the change happens. **Ponerse** + adjective is a quick change of mood, health or looks, usually temporary:

- **Se puso rojo cuando lo vieron.** (He went red when they saw him.)
- **Me pongo nervioso antes de los exámenes.** (I get nervous before exams.)
- **La niña se puso enferma el domingo.** (The girl got ill on Sunday.)
- **Se puso muy contenta con la noticia.** (She was delighted at the news.)

**Ponerse** takes an adjective, never a noun: *se puso médico* is wrong.

## Volverse and hacerse

**Volverse** + adjective is a deep, lasting change of character, often one nobody chose:

- **Con los años se volvió muy desconfiado.** (Over the years he became very distrustful.)
- **Desde que es famoso, se ha vuelto insoportable.** (Since he got famous, he's become unbearable.)
- **volverse loco** (to go mad)

**Hacerse** + noun or adjective is a change someone chooses or works for, or one that comes slowly: jobs, beliefs, money, age.

- **Se hizo médica.** (She became a doctor.)
- **Se hicieron ricos.** (They got rich.) = **se enriquecieron**
- **Nos hacemos mayores.** (We're getting older.)

A passing feeling never takes **hacerse**: *se hizo nervioso* is wrong.

## Quedarse: how things ended up

**Quedarse** + adjective, or **quedarse sin** + noun, is the state left after an event, very often a loss:

- **Se quedó ciego tras el accidente.** (He went blind after the accident.)
- **Mi tío se quedó calvo muy joven.** (My uncle went bald very young.)
- **Me quedé sin trabajo en marzo.** (I lost my job in March.)
- **Nos quedamos sin batería.** (Our battery ran out.)

It also describes being left frozen by something: **se quedó callado / sorprendido / dormido** (he fell silent / was stunned / fell asleep).

Be careful, because **quedarse** alone also means *to stay* (**me quedo en casa**). The adjective or **sin** tells you it is a change.

## Convertirse en and llegar a ser

**Convertirse en** + noun is a transformation into something else. It always takes **en**:

- **La oruga se convirtió en mariposa.** (The caterpillar turned into a butterfly.)
- **El pueblo se ha convertido en una ciudad turística.** (The village has turned into a tourist town.)

**Llegar a ser** + noun or adjective is reaching a point at the end of a long road, often after effort. It is not reflexive:

- **Llegó a ser directora del hospital.** (She eventually became head of the hospital.)
- **Con el tiempo llegaron a ser muy amigos.** (In time they became close friends.)

So use **se convirtió en** for *what* it turned into and **llegó a ser** for *how far* someone got.

vocabulary.meaning: to become, to get (a sudden, usually temporary change: + adjective)
vocabulary.example: Siempre me pongo nerviosa cuando hablo en público.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I always get nervous when I speak in public.

vocabulary.example: Se puso colorado cuando le preguntaron por su novia.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He went red when they asked him about his girlfriend.

vocabulary.meaning: to become (a deep, lasting change of character)
vocabulary.example: Desde que vive solo, se ha vuelto un poco raro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Since he started living alone, he's become a bit odd.

vocabulary.example: Después del robo, mi vecino se volvió muy desconfiado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: After the burglary, my neighbour became very distrustful.

vocabulary.meaning: to become (by choice, effort or gradually: jobs, beliefs, money, age)
vocabulary.example: Mi hermana se hizo enfermera para ayudar a la gente.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My sister became a nurse to help people.

vocabulary.meaning: to get older, to grow up
vocabulary.example: Cuando te haces mayor, valoras más el tiempo libre.
vocabulary.example_meaning: When you get older, you value free time more.

vocabulary.example: Se enriqueció vendiendo pisos en la costa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He got rich selling flats on the coast.

vocabulary.meaning: to end up, to be left (the result of an event, often a loss: + adjective)
vocabulary.example: Tras la enfermedad, se quedó sordo de un oído.
vocabulary.example_meaning: After the illness, he went deaf in one ear.

vocabulary.meaning: to be left without, to run out of, to lose
vocabulary.example: Nos quedamos sin gasolina a diez kilómetros del pueblo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We ran out of petrol ten kilometres from the village.

vocabulary.example: Mi padre se quedó calvo a los treinta años.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My father went bald at thirty.

vocabulary.meaning: to turn into, to become (+ noun)
vocabulary.example: Su afición a la cocina se convirtió en un negocio.
vocabulary.example_meaning: His love of cooking turned into a business.

vocabulary.meaning: to (eventually) become, to get to be (after a long road)
vocabulary.example: Empezó como camarero y llegó a ser dueño del restaurante.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He started as a waiter and ended up owning the restaurant.

quiz.prompt: Cuando vio la primera pregunta del examen, Luis ___ muy nervioso.
quiz.explanation: A sudden, passing feeling takes ponerse. Hacerse is for chosen or gradual changes, and convertirse en needs a noun.
hints: Is this a sudden change or a chosen one?

quiz.prompt: Cuando el profesor la felicitó delante de todos, Lucía ___ colorada. (ponerse, preterite)
quiz.explanation: Blushing is a quick, temporary change in how someone looks: ponerse colorado/a. Ella becomes se puso.
hints: Ponerse is irregular in the preterite: puse, pusiste, puso…

quiz.prompt: Después del accidente, mi abuelo ___ ciego de un ojo.
quiz.explanation: Losing your sight is the result of an event, a loss: quedarse ciego. Hacerse and llegar a ser describe changes someone chooses or works towards.
hints: Is this a goal he reached, or what was left after the accident?

quiz.prompt: Anoche ___ sin batería en mitad de la llamada. (quedarse, preterite, yo: I ran out of battery)
quiz.explanation: Running out of something is quedarse sin + noun. Yo becomes me quedé.
hints: Yo takes me plus the preterite ending -é.

quiz.prompt: Mi prima estudió siete años y ___ médica.
quiz.explanation: A profession reached by choice and study takes hacerse. Ponerse never takes a noun, and quedarse is for what is left after an event.
hints: A job is something you choose and work for.

quiz.prompt: Después de tantas mentiras, Pablo ___ muy desconfiado. (volverse, preterite)
quiz.explanation: A lasting change of character takes volverse. Él becomes se volvió.
hints: Which verb describes a change in who someone is?
Volver is regular in the preterite: volví, volviste, volvió…

quiz.prompt: Desde que se hizo famoso, Jorge ___ insoportable: ya no saluda a nadie.
quiz.explanation: A change of character takes volverse + adjective. Convertirse needs en + a noun, and quedarse describes what is left after an event, not a personality.
hints: Insoportable is an adjective about character.

quiz.prompt: El antiguo convento ___ un hotel de lujo. (convertirse en, preterite)
quiz.explanation: A transformation into something else is convertirse en + noun. Convertir has a stem change in the preterite: convirtió.
hints: Convertir becomes convirtió, like pedir becomes pidió.

quiz.prompt: Tras veinte años en el club, Andrés ___ capitán del equipo.
quiz.explanation: Reaching a position after a long road is llegar a ser, which is not reflexive. Ponerse never takes a noun.

conversations.title: The school reunion
conversations.scenario: Elena and Carlos meet at their twenty-year school reunion and catch up on how their classmates have changed.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Has visto a Raúl? Se ha hecho mayor, pero sigue igual de simpático.
lines.meaning: Have you seen Raúl? He's got older, but he's just as nice as ever.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí. ¿Sabías que se hizo abogado? Llegó a ser socio de un bufete enorme.
lines.meaning: Yes. Did you know he became a lawyer? He ended up a partner in a huge law firm.
lines.note: Hacerse for a chosen job, llegar a ser for how far he got.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Quién lo diría! En el instituto se ponía colorado cada vez que hablaba en clase.
lines.meaning: Who'd have thought it! At school he went red every time he spoke in class.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Pues ahora habla delante de jueces. ¿Y Marisa?
lines.meaning: Well, now he speaks in front of judges. What about Marisa?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Se quedó sin trabajo hace dos años, pero no se rindió.
lines.meaning: She lost her job two years ago, but she didn't give up.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Y qué hizo? Siempre hacía unas tartas buenísimas.
lines.meaning: And what did she do? She always made amazing cakes.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Exacto. Su afición se convirtió en una pastelería, la más famosa del barrio.
lines.meaning: Exactly. Her hobby turned into a cake shop, the most famous one in the neighbourhood.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Me alegro. ¿Y el profesor de química? Se volvió muy cascarrabias, ¿no?
lines.meaning: I'm glad. And the chemistry teacher? He became really grumpy, didn't he?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Un poco. Ahora se pone de mal humor si alguien llega tarde.
lines.meaning: A bit. Now he gets in a bad mood if anyone is late.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Bueno, todos cambiamos. Yo me estoy quedando calvo.
lines.meaning: Well, we all change. I'm going bald.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Y yo me pongo nerviosa en estas reuniones!
lines.meaning: And I get nervous at these reunions!

listening.note: Quedarse describes what was left, a loss.

listening.text: Con la edad se ha vuelto más tranquilo.
listening.meaning: With age he has become calmer.

listening.text: Mi vecina se hizo abogada a los cuarenta años.
listening.meaning: My neighbour became a lawyer at forty.

listening.text: El pequeño bar se convirtió en un restaurante famoso.
listening.meaning: The little bar turned into a famous restaurant.

listening.text: Cuando cerraron la fábrica, muchos se quedaron sin trabajo.
listening.meaning: When they closed the factory, many people lost their jobs.
listening.note: New word: la fábrica = the factory.

listening.text: Después de muchos años de trabajo, llegó a ser alcaldesa del pueblo.
listening.meaning: After many years of work, she became mayor of the town.
listening.note: New word: la alcaldesa = the mayor.

listening.text: Desde que trabaja de noche, mi hermano se ha vuelto un poco huraño.
listening.meaning: Since he started working nights, my brother has become a bit unsociable.

guide.tip: Ask how the change happened: in a flash (ponerse), deep inside (volverse), by choice or slowly (hacerse), as the result of an event (quedarse), into something new (convertirse en), after a long road (llegar a ser).

bites.title: Ponerse: quick and passing
bites.rule: Ponerse + adjective: a sudden, usually temporary change of mood, health or looks. Never a noun: se puso médico is wrong.
bites.example: Se puso nerviosa al ver la cámara.
bites.example_meaning: She got nervous when she saw the camera.

bites.title: Volverse: who you are
bites.rule: Volverse + adjective: a deep, lasting change in someone's character, often unwanted: se volvió desconfiado, se volvió loco.
bites.example: Con los años se volvió muy callado.
bites.example_meaning: Over the years he became very quiet.

bites.title: Hacerse: chosen or gradual
bites.rule: Hacerse + noun or adjective: a change you choose or work for, or that comes slowly: hacerse médico, rico, vegetariano, mayor.
bites.example: Se hizo profesora a los treinta años.
bites.example_meaning: She became a teacher at thirty.

bites.title: The result, the new thing, the goal
bites.rule: Quedarse: what is left, often a loss (quedarse ciego, sin trabajo). Convertirse en + noun: a transformation. Llegar a ser: the end of a long road.
bites.example: La oruga se convirtió en mariposa.
bites.example_meaning: The caterpillar turned into a butterfly.

sorts.title: What kind of change?
sorts.why: Ponerse is a flash, volverse changes who you are, hacerse is chosen or slow, quedarse is what is left after something happened.

sorts.title: Right or wrong?
sorts.why: Ponerse never takes a noun, convertirse always needs en, and llegar a ser is not reflexive.

spots.sentence: Cuando vio a su ex, Lola se hizo muy nerviosa.
spots.why: A sudden, passing feeling takes ponerse, not hacerse.

spots.sentence: Mi hermana se puso abogada el año pasado.
spots.why: A profession is a noun, and ponerse never takes a noun: se hizo abogada.

spots.sentence: La oruga se convirtió de mariposa.
spots.why: Convertirse always takes en: se convirtió en mariposa.

spots.sentence: Con mucho esfuerzo, llegó a hacer directora del banco.
spots.why: Reaching a position after a long road is llegar a ser.

spots.sentence: Desde que es rico, Jorge se ha convertido insoportable.
spots.why: A change of character with an adjective takes volverse. Convertirse needs en and a noun.

builds.text: Con los años se volvió muy desconfiado.
builds.meaning: Over the years he became very distrustful.

builds.text: Mi tío se hizo rico con un restaurante.
builds.meaning: My uncle got rich with a restaurant.

builds.text: Nos quedamos sin pan para la cena.
builds.meaning: We ran out of bread for dinner.

builds.text: El pueblo se convirtió en una ciudad.
builds.meaning: The village turned into a city.
